note: Made by the steps in TV_PICTURES.md: the chapter is split into sections that each carry one deep meaning ("sections"), 10 picture ideas are written for each, the top two for each picture are made and the better is chosen by eye (2026-11-22). Wide pictures only (1920x1088); the "tall" names are kept for the day tall pictures are switched back on. Each scene starts at the first word of its verse, or at its "from" words inside the verse. The important part of every picture sits in the upper two thirds, clear of the words. God is not pictured, Job is not portrayed as a biblical person but shown through an ordinary grey-haired man of today, and nothing violent is shown. The longing for death in this chapter is shown through darkness, silence and rest, never through any act of harm, and no infant is shown in danger.
method: Second method, asked for by Obay on 2026-11-21 after the sentence-by-sentence pictures did not connect: (1) split the chapter into sections that each carry one deep meaning, written as one plain sentence; (2) write 10 different picture ideas for each section; (3) judge them: which shows the deep meaning most truly, then which a watcher understands at once while hearing the words, then which is most engaging; (4) make the top two for each picture slot as real pictures ("candidates") and choose by eye. A section has one or two pictures. What he said went wrong before: he could not tell why some pictures were there, could not connect them to the meaning, and some were too abstract.

sections.meaning: Job breaks his silence and curses the day he was born, wishing that day had been swallowed by darkness and never lit.
ideas: A grey-haired man lays face down a framed photograph of himself as a newborn baby
A grey-haired man tears in two an old photograph of himself as a newborn
A total eclipse turns midday to night over a quiet farm valley
A huge black storm cloud settles low over the land at noon and swallows the sun
A grey-haired man draws heavy curtains shut against the morning sun
A man tears the sheet for one day off a wall calendar and crumples it
A birthday candle blown out, its smoke trailing into the dark
A sunrise swallowed by a wall of black cloud before it can light the fields
An old man sits on the edge of a bed in a dark room, head bowed, a baby photograph in his hand
A hospital nursery window at night with every light switched off

sections.meaning: He wants the night he was conceived to be barren and forgotten, with no joy and no dawn, because it did not spare him the misery he now sees.
ideas: A deserted fairground at night with every light out, the big wheel dark and still
A street of houses at night, every one lit for a celebration except one house in total darkness
A barren, cracked field under a black night sky
A grey-haired man at a window before dawn stares out at a black, starless sky with no light on the horizon
A wide dark landscape under a sky without a single star, the horizon black where the dawn should be
A grey-haired man covers his eyes with his hand and turns away from what he sees
An empty dance hall at night, chairs stacked, decorations hanging in the dark
A front door standing open on a dark night, wind blowing leaves into the house
A man sitting up through the night beside a lamp that has gone out
A patch of night sky where the stars are going out one by one

sections.meaning: He asks why he did not die at birth, for then he would be lying quiet and at rest with the great ones of the earth, whose palaces and gold now lie in ruins.
ideas: The great hall of an abandoned mansion: gilded chairs under dust, a broken chandelier, tarnished silver, light through broken windows
A row of grand old stone tombs with heavy bronze doors in a quiet cemetery under tall trees
A grey-haired man lies awake on his back in a dim bedroom, longing for sleep
A perfectly still lake at dusk with not a ripple
An overgrown palace garden, its fountains dry and its statues fallen
A rich man's vault standing open on empty shelves
Gold coins half buried in the sand of a deserted beach
A grand old house half swallowed by ivy and trees
A tired old man asleep in an armchair at last, a blanket over him
An empty bassinet in a quiet room

sections.meaning: In death the troubled and the troublers fall quiet alike: the worn-out rest, the prisoner hears no taskmaster, small and great lie together, and the slave is free.
ideas: Heavy iron shackles hang open and empty beside a door standing wide open onto quiet daylight
A grand marble monument and a small plain wooden grave marker side by side under one tree
A worn-out labourer asleep under a shade tree, his heavy load set down beside him
A factory floor at evening, the machines silent and the workers gone home
A king and a pawn lying together in the same box after the game
A bird flying out of an open cage
An empty prison yard with the gate standing open
Polished dress shoes and worn work boots side by side at a door
A heavy pack dropped on the ground at the end of a long trail
A foreman's whistle hanging silent on a nail in an empty yard

sections.meaning: He asks why life and light are given to the miserable who long for death and cannot find it, to a man whose way is hidden and whom God has hemmed in.
ideas: Seen from a little above, a grey-haired man stands walled in on every side by a tall hedge with no way out
A grey-haired man sits slumped in a dark corner with his eyes shut while bright morning sunlight floods the floor up to his feet
A man stands at a dead end in a high-walled alley
A man on a path that vanishes into fog
A weary man sits alone on a park bench while a bright summer day goes on around him
A man in a hedge maze where every path ends in a wall
A man sits in a room with every curtain drawn while the sun blazes outside
A man holding a map on a road that has been washed away
A caged songbird in a sunny window
A man at the bottom of a deep well looking up at the bright circle of sky

sections.meaning: Groaning has become his daily bread, the thing he dreaded has come upon him, and he has no ease, no quiet and no rest, only turmoil.
ideas: A grey-haired man sits at a kitchen table with his face in his hands beside an untouched plate of bread
A grey-haired man lies awake at night in twisted sheets, staring at the ceiling
Rain pours off a roof in a torrent
A man at a window watches the storm he feared arrive
A sea in turmoil, waves crashing in a gale
A man paces a dark hallway at night
A cup of coffee gone cold beside a man staring at nothing
Hands gripping grey hair
A stale loaf on a table and a man weeping
A house shaken by storm wind at night with one light on

candidates.prompt: At a plain wooden table in a dim, quiet room, a grey-haired man in a plain shirt, his face drawn with grief, is laying a small framed photograph face down on the table with one hand. The frame is still tilted up toward us, so the photograph in it can be seen: a newborn baby wrapped in a white hospital blanket. Grey daylight from a window falls on his face and on the frame.

In a dim, quiet room, a grey-haired man in a plain shirt holds up an old faded photograph of a newborn baby wrapped in a white blanket, and is tearing it slowly in two with both hands, his face twisted with grief. Grey daylight from a window falls on his face and on the photograph.

A total eclipse of the sun at midday: high in the sky the sun is a black disc ringed with thin white fire, and the whole wide valley of farms and fields below has fallen into a deep, eerie twilight, as if the day had been turned into night. Only a faint pale glow lies along the far horizon.

At midday over a wide valley of farms and fields, a huge, low, black cloud has settled over the whole land and swallowed the sun, so that the day has gone dark. Only a thin last edge of daylight shows far off at the horizon, and the fields lie in deep shadow under the cloud.

A small-town fairground at night, completely deserted. The big wheel, the carousel and the rows of stalls stand dark and still, with every light switched off and not a single bulb lit. A few streamers lie on the empty ground. Faint moonlight shows their shapes against a deep blue night sky.

A quiet street of houses at night. Every house along the street glows warmly, with lit windows and strings of festive lights, as if each were holding a celebration, except one house in the middle, which stands completely dark, with not a single light in any window.

Inside a dark room before dawn, a grey-haired man in a plain shirt stands at a tall window with one hand on the frame, seen from slightly behind and to the side, staring out at a black night sky with not a single star in it. Far out over the dark fields the horizon shows no glow of dawn at all. Only a faint cold light falls on his face and his hand.

A wide, empty landscape of dark fields and low hills in the last hour of night, under a sky without a single star. Low over the far horizon, where the dawn should be breaking, there is no light at all, only black cloud. The faintest cold grey shows the outline of the hills.

The great hall of a grand old mansion, long abandoned and utterly silent. Gilded chairs and a long banquet table stand under thick dust, a huge crystal chandelier hangs broken and crooked from the ceiling, gold-framed mirrors hang askew on the walls, and tarnished silver dishes and candlesticks stand on the table. Soft shafts of daylight fall through tall broken windows with ivy growing in.

A row of grand old stone family tombs, each like a small stately house with carved pillars and heavy bronze doors, stands in a quiet old cemetery under tall trees. Moss and ivy grow over them and fallen leaves lie on their steps. Soft, still afternoon light; everything is peaceful and silent.

Inside an old stone room, a pair of heavy iron shackles joined by a chain hangs open and empty from an iron hook on the wall, right beside a heavy wooden door that stands wide open onto bright, quiet daylight and green fields. Dust floats in the light. Everything is still.

In a quiet country graveyard under one great spreading tree, a tall, grand, polished marble monument stands right beside a small plain wooden grave marker, the two side by side in the same soft grass, sharing the same shade. Peaceful late-afternoon light; a few wildflowers in the grass.

Seen from a little above, a grey-haired man in a plain shirt stands alone on a small patch of grass that is walled in on every side by a tall, thick, dark green hedge far higher than his head, with no gap, gate or path out anywhere. He stands facing the hedge with his empty hands hanging at his sides. Bright daylight falls on him from above.

A grey-haired man in a plain shirt sits slumped in a chair in the dark corner of a bare room, his eyes shut and his face turned away, while a broad beam of bright morning sunlight pours in through a window and floods across the floor right up to his feet.

At a plain kitchen table in grey morning light, a grey-haired man in a plain shirt sits with his face buried in his hands. In front of him a plate with a piece of bread and a glass of water stand untouched.

At night in a dim bedroom, lit faintly by a streetlight through the curtains, a grey-haired man lies on his back in a tangle of twisted sheets, wide awake, staring up at the ceiling, worn out and unable to rest.
